newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hochtief finds detour to Holzmann -report.
newsitem.headline: Hochtief finds detour to Holzmann -report.

text.p: German construction firm Hochtief AG has found a legal detour to gain control over its rival Philipp Holzmann AG, by pooling its shares with Deutsche Bank, the weekly magazine Focus reported.

Under the plan, RWE AG unit Hochtief would not expand its holdings of Holzmann beyond 24.9 percent, but it is about to sign a contract with Deutsche Bank, which holds 25.8 percent, that will allow it to get around the objections of German cartel authorities, the magazine said.
The agreement would not be subject to the approval of German cartel authorities, but of European Union authorities who are seen as more sympathetic, the magazine said.
A Deutsche Bank official declined to comment on the report. Officials at Hochtief and Holzmann were not available for comment at the weekend.
German cartel authorities, which last year blocked Hochtief's bid to take over Holzmann, last Wednesday postponed until April 9 their first hearings on greater cooperation between the two.
Holzmann has resisted Hochtief's efforts to take control of it, but the two have been planning greater cooperation, particularly outside Germany.
Hochtief had earlier planned to raise its stake in Holzmann to 35 percent from 20 percent.
